verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents sync scheduling (cron/scheduled/manual), a Connection Timeline showing historical sync events/errors, and a notification system for important events (email/webhook) — these provide the raw signals needed to infer table freshness and catch failures. However there is no documented feature that explicitly computes/display 'freshness' per destination table or proactively warns when a pipeline misses its expected cadence (e.g., an SLA/staleness alert), so analytics engineers would need to build this monitoring themselves on top of the timeline/notifications. Missing for 10: a native freshness metric per table, explicit 'missed cadence' SLA alerting, and any independent/hands-on evidence that these signals are used this way in practice.
